name: Spaciousness · VBT vv. 43–48

summary.text: The spaciousness dhāraṇās of the Vijñāna Bhairava, in Satsang’s words: notice the space of the room, then the space inside the chest, mouth and skull, feel the skin as a thin wall with open space on both sides, and rest in one field of space.

needs_teacher.note: a safe dhāraṇā; the rest of the text is teacher-gated

needs_teacher_note: Safe contemplative dhāraṇā; retention, mantra and subtle-body practices of the VBT are learned from a teacher in the Trika tradition.

steps.text: Notice the space of the room around you, holding the walls and your body.
Sense the space inside the body: the chest, the mouth, the skull.
Feel the skin as a thin wall, open space within and without.
Let inner and outer space be one field; rest in that openness. When the mind reaches for something solid, return to space. Stay alert.

contraindications.text: If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious: open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.
A history of trauma, dissociation, psychosis or severe anxiety: keep sits short with eyes open, or practise with a qualified teacher or clinician.

value.when: if space feels unsettling: a body-based breath practice
